Apple's macOS developer beta has moved from beta 4 to beta 5 after a three-week gap, and now just a week after that release on Monday of last week, the sixth beta has arrived. Here's what's in this build.

Apple Seeds macOS 27 Developer Beta 6

As we inch closer to the release version, Apple is now seeding the sixth beta of macOS 27 Golden Gate to developers.

Last week's beta 5 brought refreshed icons for several apps including Siri, Chess, and Safari, but didn't include any new features (or notable bugs).

macOS 27 Golden Gate features a dedicated Siri app, unified rounded corner design for windows and apps, and AI-driven features for Shortcuts and Safari that let users build extensions and automations with simple commands.

The system also adds a new "pull to refresh" gesture in Safari, which many see as Apple laying the groundwork for the rumored touchscreen MacBook Pro, making macOS more touch-friendly.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also overhauls iPhone Mirroring with the ability to resize windows to different aspect ratios, which is also seen as preparation for the rumored foldable iPhone Ultra expected to be announced next month.

The build number for macOS 27 Golden Gate is 26A5416b.

Installing the macOS 27 Golden Gate beta

Here's how to install the macOS 27 Golden Gate developer beta 5:

  • Back up your Mac
  • Open System Settings
  • Go to General → Software Update
  • Click the "i" next to Beta Updates
  • From the drop-down in the top right, choose "macOS Developer Golden Gate Beta"
  • Click Done

Have you found any new features in this macOS 27 Golden Gate beta? Drop them in the comments.
